title: The Resolve to Grow Stronger
text: “Yeah…”
“You know… it might be selfish of me to say this, but don’t you think Wyndia-chan’s father just wants her to grow into a dragon he can be proud of, no matter where she goes?”
Father was trying his best to get Assistant motivated, but her response was remarkably dull.
“Hmm… well, I get that it’s worrying when you realize your dad’s actually weak. So how about this—what if we all helped Wyndia-chan get stronger?”
The moment he suggested that, Assistant lifted her head, apparently interested.
“So that if something happens, you’ll be able to protect your dad.”
“Yeah… that’s right. Dad’s weak, so I’ll get strong, and I’ll take over the territory and protect him!”

At that moment, the egg’s steady heartbeat seemed to skip ever so slightly, or so it looked to me. So it was going this way again, was it? In the loop where we all headed to Faubrey together, Assistant’s goal had been to get strong enough to make everyone eat their words. But in this loop, it seemed the flow was shifting toward her deciding to grow strong out of worry that Rival’s parent was simply too weak. Somehow this version had even less dignity to it. And I already knew for a fact that things would sink even lower once Rival actually showed up.
“W-well, that’s the spirit, I suppose? Fortunately—or something—you’re going to have a little brother or sister hatching from that egg, right?”

“Yeah! Dad asked me whether I wanted a brother or a sister, so I said I wanted a sister. I’m going to grow strong together with her and raise her into a splendid dragon who can protect Dad! I’ve decided!”

Somehow Assistant seemed far hungrier for strength than in any previous loop. No, actually—her personality now felt closer to how she’d been after Rival left Shieldfreeden. It seemed that in this loop too, Rival’s pathetic parent was destined to end up getting strengthened by us.
“Um, Hero-sama… Imiya thinks she should get stronger too. Is that… is that all right?”
Caught up in Assistant’s burning spirit, Mole turned to ask Father.
“You don’t need to worry about that, Imiya-chan.”
“But…”
Father gently stroked Mole’s head.
“Imiya-chan. What matters most to me is that you grow up healthy and happy.”
“Y-yes…”

Mole obediently accepted Father’s words. And yet, I noticed her fists were clenched tight all the same. Incidentally, Mole had apparently gotten along well with Keel too, and the two of them had started joining Crocodile Guy’s training sessions together, both wanting to grow stronger. Father never asked anything of her directly, and yet she still craved strength all the same. It seemed that watching Big Sister—watching how things were when it was just her alone with Father—had planted the same thought in Mole’s heart.
“Mmn… oh, Wyndia-chan, are you awake?”
“Mmm… GWAAAAAAH! Luna! Did you put me to sleep in front of Keel again?!”
And so, right as I was talking with Assistant, Keel and Ren woke up and began voicing their complaints. Incidentally, Ren still looked half-asleep, squinting his eyes even as he fumed.
“Mmm… oh, Keel-kun and the others are up, so cute… Luna’s up too… zzz.”
“You’re asleep again!”
“Just stay asleep forever!”
Assistant glared at Luna-chan with open displeasure. What was that about, I wondered? Did she have some sort of grudge against Luna-chan?
“Alright everyone, let’s do proper introductions. Nice to meet you all going forward.”
“Yeah! Nice to meet ya!”
“Likewise, pleased to meet you.”
“Hmph… well, the people here will lend you strength, so speak up if anything happens. That egg’s about to hatch soon too, isn’t it?”
Ren said this to Assistant with a rather condescending air. Assistant looked between Keel, Ren, and Mole before nodding.

“Yeah. Nice to meet you all. Thank you for playing with me, and for worrying about me enough to come all the way up the mountain. I never thought… I never thought anyone would worry about me. I thought everyone would just end up killed by my dad, so I couldn’t even tell anyone… I’m sorry.”
“It’s all good! Don’t worry about it. Besides, we ended up beating your dad black and blue anyway, didn’t we—”
Ren placed a hand on Keel’s shoulder as though worried about what she’d just said, silently urging her not to provoke things further.
“Yeah. I actually realized my dad’s weak, so I’m gonna get strong! I’m going to protect him by getting stronger! Otherwise he’s going to end up killed somewhere out there!”
“Ugh…”
Ren pressed a hand to his chest at that. He was probably thinking, from the bottom of his heart, how glad he was that the planned dragon extermination hadn’t gone through after all.
“Yeah! Got it! I wanna get stronger too, so let’s do it together!”
“Yeah!”
Keel and Assistant seemed to hit it off splendidly like that.
“Sword bro, you gotta get stronger too.”
“Ah, ah…”
Is this really okay? Ren tilted his head, glancing over toward Father as if asking. Then he turned back to Assistant and raised his fist.
“Right. I’ll get strong enough to send an army of Filolials packing in defeat! Together with that dragon egg of yours! So that nobody can drag me off while I’m sleeping ever again!”
“Yeah!”

For some reason, Assistant raised her fist right along with him in agreement. I found myself thinking that the gentle Father from some other loop would probably watch this exchange between Assistant and Ren with a knowing grin, comparing it to how things had gone with other versions of Ren. It had turned into a relationship you didn’t often see, that much was certain.
“So once that egg hatches, what are you gonna name it? Wyndia-chan.”
“I’m just gonna use Dad’s name as it is… Gaelion! The strongest dragon gets to have Dad’s name!”
So that was the one thing she wouldn’t budge on.
“Wouldn’t Jak—short for Jack, from ‘weakest’—suit your parent better, I say?”
That would make a fitting second name for your parent to go by. Though it would have to be crammed rather compactly!
“No way! I hate that name!”
“Ahaha… well, Ren, please look after Wyndia-chan for us.”

“Yeah. Sure. I’ll raise her in their place. First thing’s figuring out where to teach her to hunt… Since it turns out there are some differences in how our strengthening methods work, maybe a two-stage jump would be the way to go…”

And so Assistant and Rival’s parent officially joined our ranks. Ren raising her was more than a little worrying. We’d need to make sure she didn’t end up getting killed fighting something like Spirit Tortoise, at the very least. Still, it seemed some of the strengthening methods could now be shared between us, and after experiencing training alongside Father’s slaves and Éclair, they seemed to be searching for ways to raise the bar further. Well, worst case, Assistant seemed to be on good terms with Father as well, so even without becoming a slave, some manner of aptitude reinforcement ought to be possible. And so, at Rival’s parent’s own request, Assistant and Father were registered as the primary bond-holders, and from the empty shell of an egg that Rival’s parent had inhabited, Rival’s actual body finally hatched.
“…Gyaow.”
“So it’s a girl, right?”
“Yes.”
Assistant nodded, going along with the flow as she confirmed the parent now residing in Rival’s newly hatched body.
“Huh? The name’s already decided? Were you listening to what we were just talking about?”
“Gyaow!”
Shameless, that one, inhabiting a child’s body and pulling this baby-play act without so much as batting an eye. What a pervert, possessing an infant like that.
“Chirp!”

Luna-chan had transformed into her chick form and perched atop Keel—truly, Filolial-sama are adorable creatures. Incidentally, we’d already finished off Takt’s dragon, so we had plenty of core stones secured. Whether we’d actually hand any over was another matter entirely. In any case, however displeased I was, however much I wanted to keep my distance, Rival’s parent had ended up joining us alongside Assistant regardless. Naturally, Assistant was devouring the breakfast Father and the others had prepared like she couldn’t get enough of it. Since Rival’s parent and Filolial-sama didn’t get along, the plan seemed to be keeping them on separate schedules. Since Ren, having hit it off with them, would mainly be handling the training, it looked like I wouldn’t need to get too deeply involved either.
